title: Some important new statistical findings
publication: New Research on the Voynich Manuscript: Proceedings of a Seminar
main_result: Two statistically distinct textual populations called A and B
claimed_interpretation: Statistical clustering may reflect two languages or systems

authors: Friedman, William F.; Friedman, Elizebeth S.
title: Voynich study-group materials and cryptanalytic correspondence
main_result: No published validated decipherment in the consulted archival descriptions

title: Evidence of linguistic structure in the Voynich manuscript using spectral analysis
main_result: Reports spectral regularities interpreted as linguistic structure
claimed_interpretation: Language-like structure is argued, but cipher/generator controls were not the central comparison

title: Voynich manuscript: statistical properties of the Voynich text
main_result: Publishes token, glyph, positional, and vocabulary statistics
claimed_interpretation: Descriptive resource; it does not establish H_L, H_C, or H_G

title: What We Know About The Voynich Manuscript
publication: Proceedings of the 5th ACL-HLT Workshop on Language Technology for Cultural Heritage, Social Sciences, and Humanities
main_result: Multiple standard linguistic tests are compatible with language and several cipher models
claimed_interpretation: Compatibility tests do not identify a language or prove a ciphertext

authors: Montemurro, Marcelo A.; Zanette, Damián H.
title: Keywords and Co-Occurrence Patterns in the Voynich Manuscript: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
main_result: Word co-occurrence and extracted keywords are non-random and section-associated
claimed_interpretation: Authors interpret this as evidence for semantic content; generator controls are absent

title: The Voynich Manuscript: Evidence of the Hoax Hypothesis
main_result: Reports unusual repetition, line-position, and distributional features
claimed_interpretation: Features are argued to favour fabricated text; a generator is not by itself a no-message proof

title: A possible generating algorithm of the Voynich manuscript
main_result: Self-citation/copy-and-modify generation reproduces selected frequency and similarity properties
claimed_interpretation: Selected language-like properties are not specific to a message

title: The Linguistics of the Voynich Manuscript
main_result: Reviews linguistic arguments and their limits
claimed_interpretation: Secondary synthesis; not entered as primary evidence

title: Character Entropy in Modern and Historical Texts: Comparison Metrics for an Undeciphered Manuscript
main_result: Voynich conditional character entropy is atypical relative to their comparison corpora
claimed_interpretation: Representation and comparator choice constrain any class-level conclusion

authors: Sterneck, Rachel; Polish, Annie; Bowern, Claire
title: Topic Modeling in the Voynich Manuscript
main_result: Topic models recover page clusters associated with illustration sections
claimed_interpretation: Section association is compatible with content but lacks a structured-generator control

title: Enciphered after all? Word-level text metrics are compatible with some types of encipherment
publication: Proceedings of the 2022 International Voynich Conference (CEUR-WS)
main_result: Some word-level metrics survive/recur under tested encipherment schemes
claimed_interpretation: Word-level language tests do not exclude all cipher families

title: The Naibbe cipher: a substitution cipher that encrypts Latin and Italian as Voynich Manuscript-like ciphertext
corpus/transcription: Latin/Italian synthetic plaintext and Voynich comparison
main_result: A specified cipher produces several Voynich-like statistics from known plaintext
claimed_interpretation: Statistical resemblance demonstrates mechanism compatibility, not the manuscript's plaintext

title: A Glyph Is Not a Letter, a Token Is Not a Word, a Space Is Not a Space
main_result: Adjacent token order carries a very small corrected share while edge coupling remains structured
claimed_interpretation: Visible glyph/token/space units must not be assumed to be linguistic units

title: A Quantitative Confirmation of the Currier Language Distinction
main_result: Quantitative classifier recovers the established A/B partition
claimed_interpretation: A/B is a reproducible statistical distinction, not demonstrated evidence for two languages

title: Polygraphiae libri sex
main_result: Codebook/table-mediated substitution demonstrates the distinction between ciphertext and external key/table
claimed_interpretation: Historical analogue only; no Voynich inference
